skill.summary: Coordinate structured incident response workflows from alert triage through postmortem follow-up.

content.value_statement: Production incidents require fast triage, clear ownership, and controlled recovery. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured SRE response workflow.
actual_capabilities: Classifies incidents using P0 through P3 severity levels.
Guides detection, triage, observability review, mitigation, recovery, and postmortem work.
Defines prompts for incident, observability, debugging, security, performance, deployment, and documentation subagents.
Provides communication roles, handoff rules, and stakeholder update guidance.
Lists immediate and long-term success criteria for incident response.
limitations: Does not connect to monitoring, paging, deployment, or ticketing systems by itself.
Requires accurate incident context, logs, metrics, and operator authorization.
Does not replace live incident commander decisions or compliance review.
Needs adaptation to organization-specific severity policies and tooling.

use_cases.title: Triage a Production Outage
use_cases.description: Classify severity, assess user impact, assign roles, and identify immediate mitigation steps.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Recovery Work
use_cases.description: Organize debugging, security review, deployment validation, communication, and rollback readiness.

use_cases.title: Create Postmortem Actions
use_cases.description: Document the timeline, root cause, lessons learned, prevention work, and monitoring improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Classify This Incident
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner triage for a new alert.
prompt_templates.prompt: Classify this incident using the skill workflow: [describe alert, affected service, symptoms, and known user impact].

prompt_templates.title: Run Observability Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate investigation after severity is known.
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide an observability sweep for this incident: [severity, service, time range, metrics, logs, traces, and recent changes].

prompt_templates.title: Plan Mitigation and Updates
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a mitigation, validation, rollback, and stakeholder communication plan for this incident: [current findings and constraints].

prompt_templates.title: Lead Full Lifecycle Response
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced response from detection through prevention.
prompt_templates.prompt: Coordinate the full incident lifecycle for this event: [timeline, services, severity, evidence, actions taken, risks, and owners].

output_examples.input: API error rate increased after a deployment, affecting checkout for one region.
output: Severity: P1 because customer checkout is degraded for a significant segment.
Immediate actions: pause rollout, compare metrics before and after deployment, and prepare rollback.
Communication: provide internal updates every 15 minutes until stability returns.

output_examples.input: Database latency spiked, and customer support reports delayed account updates.
output: Investigation focus: query performance, locks, dependency queues, and recent schema changes.
Mitigation focus: reduce write pressure, scale resources if authorized, and protect critical paths.
Follow-up: document customer impact, assign action items, and improve latency alerts.

output_examples.input: A resolved outage needs a postmortem and prevention plan.
output: Postmortem should include timeline, root cause, contributing factors, decisions, and customer impact.
Prevention work should include monitoring changes, runbook updates, and resilience improvements.
Owners and deadlines should be assigned for each action item.

best_practices: Confirm severity, scope, owner, and customer impact before assigning detailed investigation work.
Keep mitigation, validation, communication, and rollback decisions visible in one shared incident record.
Convert postmortem lessons into owned prevention tasks with deadlines.
anti_patterns: Do not use the workflow to access systems without explicit authorization.
Do not skip communication planning during active customer impact.
Do not treat generated plans as deployment approval without human review.

faq.question: What type of incidents does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports outages, performance degradation, security incidents, data integrity issues, infrastructure failures, and third-party service disruptions.

faq.question: Can it connect to monitoring tools directly?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow guidance and prompts, but the operator must supply authorized data from monitoring tools.

faq.question: Does it replace an incident commander?
faq.answer: No. It helps structure response work, but accountable decisions remain with the incident commander and responsible teams.

faq.question: Can Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: How should teams adapt the severity levels?
faq.answer: Map P0 through P3 definitions to your organization's SLA, SLO, customer impact, and escalation policies.

faq.question: What should users provide before starting?
faq.answer: Provide the alert, affected service, time range, user impact, recent changes, known constraints, and authorized evidence sources.
